model: Market-maker net profit capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.owner_earnings_note: Owner earnings = net profit (SBC already expensed inside it); FY2022 126.8 -> FY2025 133.6 (3yr), FY2020 464.5 -> FY2025 133.6 (5yr). Reported FCF CAGRs are omitted because FCF is not a meaningful series for a market maker (FY2025 reported FCF -126.9 on net profit 133.6).
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Unchanged from the prior valuation: 3-year book-value CAGR (FY2022 606.3 -> FY2025 868.0) is the conservative anchor; it is not used directly to drive NTI, which is projected off a mid-cycle FY2026E base with structural ETF-market growth assumptions. 5-year NTI/EPS CAGRs are deeply negative only because FY2020 (NTI 933m, COVID volatility) is the start year.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year NTI/EPS CAGRs (-12% / -21%) diverge by more than 30pp from equity CAGRs (+8.0% 5yr, +12.7% 3yr). This is the FY2020 COVID-base artefact, not a structural decline; book value has compounded through the FY2023 trough. Note also that FY2026E NTI (~500) will show only ~3% growth on FY2025 after a 9M26 that was +7% YoY: 3Q26 was a drought quarter (NTI 84.5m, net profit 6.4m).
historical_growth.notes: Trading capital doubled from ~EUR 580m (FY2022) to EUR 1,137m (3Q26) while NTI rose ~9% over the same span: return on trading capital has fallen from 66-85% (2H24) to 30% (3Q26), 47% YTD26. Growth in this model therefore comes from structural ETF-market expansion (market ETF value traded +41% YTD26) rather than from further balance-sheet growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Moderate-volatility regime with structural ETF-market growth (global ETF AuM forecast ~12%/yr to 2030) only partly captured: NTI compounds ~6-7%/yr from a ~EUR 500m FY2026E mid-cycle base to ~EUR 676m by FY2031, digital assets stay a ~10-13% contributor, APAC monetisation improves slowly. Fixed opex follows the FY2026 guidance midpoint (EUR 240m) growing ~6%/yr, variable comp stays ~28% of the pool, so reported EBITDA margin holds ~37.5% -- short of the Horizon 2030 >45% ambition. Interest on the fully drawn facilities (~EUR 22m) and a 21% tax rate leave net profit rising from ~EUR 126m (FY2027) to ~EUR 160m (FY2031); the terminal value capitalises that at ~11x earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: Horizon 2030 broadly delivered, a year late: a sustained higher-volatility regime, full deployment of the EUR 1.1bn+ trading-capital base, APAC monetisation catching up with the region's +82% YTD value-traded growth, and a digital-assets / tokenised-RWA recovery lift NTI 12-16%/yr to ~EUR 960m by FY2031 (the >EUR 1bn target). Operating leverage over a fixed cost base growing 8-9%/yr carries the reported EBITDA margin to ~45%, the facilities amortise, and net profit approaches EUR 300m. Capitalised at the Gordon value (11.4x, inside the 13x cap).
scenario_narratives.bear: A prolonged volatility drought on the pattern of FY2023 and 3Q26 (VIX ~16, ETF value traded down, digital-asset volumes at multi-year lows): NTI falls ~15% in FY2027 and drifts to ~EUR 412m before a slow recovery. Fixed opex is sticky (EUR 248-272m, hiring and technology commitments already made) and interest stays ~EUR 22-23m on a fully drawn facility, so reported EBITDA margins compress to ~27-30% and net profit to ~EUR 55-70m (EPS ~EUR 1.2-1.5). The variable-comp absorber keeps the firm profitable -- breakeven needs NTI below ~EUR 280-300m -- but the market pays a trough multiple (9x cap) and the stock can sit at or below this value for extended stretches, as it did through FY2023.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Flow Traders is a proprietary market maker whose reported cash flow is meaningless for valuation (FY2025 OCF EUR -120.6m in a EUR 133.6m net-income year, purely trading-capital working capital), so this model discounts projected NET PROFIT at a 12% EUR cost of equity, in the spirit of a bank/broker earnings-at-cost-of-equity framework, with trading capital treated as a required operating asset (net debt held at zero, interest charged inside the flows) and the terminal value capped at a cyclical-appropriate exit P/E (11x base / 13x bull / 9x bear). Earnings are volatility-dependent with no revenue floor -- NTI can move 30-50% quarter to quarter -- so the discipline is (1) a mid-cycle NTI base (~EUR 500m FY2026E, not the annualised H1 run-rate of 607 nor the 3Q26 drought pace of 338), (2) margins built from the cost structure (guided fixed opex plus a ~28% variable-comp share of the pool) rather than carried forward, (3) SBC charged exactly once through an explicit line against a pre-SBC margin with a flat fully diluted share count, and (4) risk charged once -- in scenario flows weighted 25/50/25, at a single cost of equity, not again through per-scenario discount rates. The base value is a mid-cycle fair value, not a price target: in low-volatility regimes the stock trades at or below the bear value for long stretches (FY2023), and in volatility spikes well above the bull (FY2020). The weighted value is only actionable alongside the bear value and the current return on trading capital.
key_risks_to_valuation: Volatility regime: NTI has no floor; 3Q26 (NTI EUR 84.5m, EBITDA margin 20%, net profit EUR 6.4m) shows a single quiet quarter removes most of a year's earnings growth. The base assumes a mid-cycle average, which no single year delivers.

Operating and financial leverage: fixed opex guidance EUR 235-245m (+15-20% on FY2025) and ~EUR 22m/yr interest on the SOFR+500bps facility raise the NTI level needed for any given margin; the variable-comp absorber limits but does not remove this.
Digital assets: 13% of YTD26 NTI versus 26% a year earlier, down 46% YTD; a continued crypto downturn delays the tokenisation leg of Horizon 2030.

Return on trading capital has fallen from 66-85% (2H24) to 30% (3Q26) while capital doubled; if the expanded balance sheet cannot be deployed at historical returns, the base growth path overstates earnings capacity.
Competition from private mega-firms (Citadel Securities, Jane Street, Optiver) with far larger scale and no disclosure constraints; the Horizon 2030 plan is public.

Capital return suspended through 2030: value accrues only through retained trading capital, so the terminal exit multiple carries 60-70% of value and a persistent discount (P/E 8-10x has been the norm since 2022) would leave the weighted value unrealised.
Terminal-multiple sensitivity: each 1x change in the base exit-P/E cap moves the base value by roughly EUR 2/share.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E net trading income (NTI): 9M26 actual EUR 388.2m (3Q26 trading update, 29 Oct 2026) plus a Q4 estimate of ~EUR 112m, pitched between the drought-like 3Q26 (EUR 84.5m, VIX 16.0) and 4Q25 (EUR 123.8m). ~EUR 500m is a mid-cycle base on the current EUR 1.1bn trading-capital base: FY2022 460, FY2023 300 (drought), FY2024 468, FY2025 486. It deliberately replaces the EUR 607m annualised-H1 run-rate adopted in the 2026-08-28 correction, which Q3 showed to be a peak-half extrapolation. Revenue in this model is NTI; the Metrics.csv revenue column is NTI.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: H1-2026 interim note 6 weighted-average diluted shares 45,680,726 (basic 43,989,843 + 1,690,883 dilutive share-based awards). 3Q26 basic weighted average 44,072,124. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (inside employee expenses and charged again explicitly via sbc_pct_path on a pre-SBC margin) -- charging the expense AND compounding the count would double-count. This replaces the prior model's 44.0m basic count grown 1.0%/yr; by Y5 the two converge (45.7 vs 46.2).
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO by design. Loans and borrowings of EUR 197.5m at 30-Jun-2026 ($200m private credit facility at SOFR+500bps plus $75m revolver, drawn to fund the trading-capital expansion) finance trading capital (EUR 1,137m at 30-Sep-2026), which is required regulatory/operating capital, not distributable surplus -- the same logic as a bank's funding. Their cost (interest ~EUR 22m/yr run-rate; 3Q26 EUR 5.4m) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path, so the flow discounted is post-interest net profit and the debt must not be deducted again. Balance-sheet cash of EUR 6.9m is likewise part of trading capital and is not added.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner earnings = FY2026E net profit: 9M26 actual EUR 97.6m plus Q4E ~EUR 20m. For a principal market maker reported FCF is a working-capital artefact of trading-capital deployment (FY2025 reported FCF EUR -126.9m in a EUR 133.6m net-income year), so the flow this model discounts is net profit, and the engine is configured (capex = D&A, no working-capital capture) so that its 'owner FCF' line equals projected net profit.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 reported free cash flow (OCF -120.6 less capex 6.3), shown for audit only; not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FLOW.AS_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 EUR 17.6m (equity-settled share-based payment transactions EUR 11.7m per FY2025 AR statement of changes in equity, line 3986, plus cash-settled component). No equity-award withholding taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). Share-based pay sits inside 'variable employee expenses' in reported EBITDA; the ebitda_margin_path below is therefore stated PRE-SBC (reported margin + 3.5pp) and SBC is charged once, explicitly, through sbc_pct_path.
inputs.buyback_note: No buyback in FY2025 or 9M26 (FY2024: EUR 11.8m). Dividends and buybacks suspended through at least 2030 under Horizon 2030; capital is retained as trading capital. The flat count is a modelling convention the company is not funding with repurchases; dilution from vesting is captured by using the diluted count.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T16:36:19Z regular close, Euronext Amsterdam (last bar before the 2026-11-02 valuation; 52-week range 21.80-30.48; the stock fell ~10% over 29-30 Oct on the 3Q26 trading update)
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-06-30 (H1-2026 interim: loans & borrowings, cash, equity, diluted shares); trading capital EUR 1,137m as at 2026-09-30 per the 3Q26 trading update, which carries no balance sheet
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 12.0%, built in EUR (the flows' own currency): 10-year Bund ~3.3% (mid-2026) + equity risk premium 5.5% x beta ~1.45 (volatility-dependent earnings with no revenue floor; NTI swings 30-50% QoQ, 3Q26 -43% QoQ) = ~11.3%, plus ~0.7% small/mid-cap Euronext illiquidity premium. Applied as a SINGLE rate to all three scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in per-scenario discount rates (the prior model used 11%/12%/14% bull/base/bear; that stacking is removed here as a deliberate methodology alignment -- see reconciliation).
inputs.lease_treatment: lease_cost_pct_path is used as the FINANCING CHARGE inside EBIT, not for property leases: it carries interest on the credit facilities (~EUR 22m/yr; 9M26 EUR 15.2m, 3Q26 EUR 5.4m) plus IFRS 16 lease interest (~EUR 1.6m/yr), expressed as a % of NTI (a fixed EUR cost, so the % falls as NTI grows and rises in the bear). Right-of-use depreciation sits in reported D&A, and capex is set equal to D&A, so the lease principal is charged exactly once through the D&A/capex line. Lease liabilities (EUR 42.2m at FY2025) are therefore NOT added to net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no minority interests; net profit is wholly attributable to ordinary shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: net profit (owner earnings) discounted at the cost of equity with an exit-P/E cap -- the prior valuation's model (model_type 'earnings_based_cost_of_equity', 2026-08-01), kept for comparability. ROUTING: Flow Traders is a principal trading firm / electronic market maker with no client AuM and no recurring revenue; its cash-flow statement is dominated by trading-capital working capital, so the owner-FCF DCF's inputs (FCF, net debt, EV/EBITDA) do not mean what that engine assumes. The dcf-methods routing table has no explicit market-maker row; the nearest analogue is the broker/financial 'earnings or FCFE at cost of equity, net debt = 0' treatment (6099.HK), which is what this file implements through the engine. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = NTI; ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC (reported EBITDA margin + 3.5pp) with SBC charged via sbc_pct_path; lease_cost_pct_path = interest on borrowings + lease interest; da_pct_path = capex_pct_path so FCF = net profit; wc_capture_pct = 0; net_debt = 0; wacc = cost of equity; terminal_cap_multiple = exit P/E cap (11x base / 13x bull / 9x bear, as prior). MARGINS are built from the prior model's cost structure: fixed opex at the FY2026 guidance midpoint (EUR 240m, reaffirmed 29-Oct-2026) growing ~6%/yr in base and bull, sticky in the bear; variable employee expense held at ~28% of (NTI - fixed opex) (FY2025 ~27-29%, 9M26 27.9%); reported EBITDA = 0.72 x (NTI - fixed opex). The historical Actuals sheet shows POST-SBC EBITDA margins (FY2025 41.4%), so compare them with the model's pre-SBC path less 3.5pp. HORIZON: 5 years FY2027-FY2031 from an FY2026E base (10 months of FY2026 are known); the prior ran FY2026-FY2030 from FY2025.

bear.growth_note: Volatility drought: FY2027 NTI falls to ~425 and FY2028 to ~412 before a slow recovery (420 / 433 / 446). The first two years are re-judged on the 3Q26 evidence -- a quarter at EUR 84.5m NTI (EUR 338m annualised) inside an otherwise normal year shows the drought run-rate on today's capital base; the prior bear (-5/-2 from 485.8, trough ~452) predates that print. The trough is set above the annualised 3Q26 pace because the prior's variable-comp absorber analysis stands: breakeven needs NTI below ~280-300. Later years (+2/+3/+3) are the prior's.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: PRE-SBC. Reported 30.0 / 27.6 / 27.4 / 27.8 / 28.1% from sticky fixed opex 248 / 254 / 260 / 266 / 272 (prior bear path: technology and AI hiring commitments already made) and variable comp at 28% of the shrunken NTI-less-fixed-opex pool. Comparable to the prior bear's 24-29% reported path and to FY2023's 22% on a smaller cost base.
bear.lease_cost_note: Interest 22 / 23 / 23 / 22 / 21m (facility stays fully drawn, slow deleveraging without earnings growth, as prior) + lease interest 1.6m, over a smaller NTI.
bear.terminal_note: 9x exit-P/E cap binds (Gordon at 12%/2% = 10.2x). Prior bear used a 14% cost of equity; a single 12% is applied here (risk charged once, in the flows).

base.growth_note: Prior base path (7.0/7.0/6.5/6.0/6.0 for FY2026-30) carried forward one year: FY2027 7.0, FY2028 6.5, FY2029 6.0, FY2030 6.0, FY2031 5.5 (new terminal year, decelerating). Captures roughly half of the ~12%/yr ETF-market growth (PwC ETFs 2030) net of share pressure from Citadel Securities / Jane Street and a flat digital-assets contribution. NTI: 535 / 570 / 604 / 640 / 676.
base.ebitda_margin_note: PRE-SBC. Reported (post-SBC) margin ~37.5-37.7% = 0.72 x (NTI - fixed opex) / NTI with fixed opex 254 / 270 / 286 / 303 / 321 (FY2026 guidance midpoint 240 growing ~6%/yr, the prior path) and variable comp at 28% of NTI less fixed opex. Below the prior's 40-42% reported path purely because the NTI base is ~500 not 607; the cost structure is the prior's. Well short of the Horizon 2030 >45% ambition, which is bull territory.
base.lease_cost_note: Financing charge: interest on borrowings EUR 22m/yr (facility fully drawn; 3Q26 run-rate 21.6m) + lease interest 1.6m = 23.6m, as % of NTI.
base.da_note: D&A (incl. ROU depreciation and small intangible impairments) ~EUR 20m in FY2027 (9M26 13.1m + 1.3m impairment) rising to ~27m by FY2031 with the AI/technology build-out, as prior (19.5 -> 26.6).
base.capex_note: Set equal to D&A so the engine's owner FCF equals net profit (earnings model). Actual cash capex runs ~EUR 6-9m/yr, below D&A, so this is conservative.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 12%/2.5% implies 10.8x terminal-year net profit; the 11x exit-P/E cap (prior) sits just above it. Flow Traders' own P/E has averaged ~15x ex-outliers but was 7.8-10.3x in FY2018/FY2024/FY2025.

bull.growth_note: Prior bull rates kept unchanged (16/15/14/13/12). Off the lower ~500 base the path reaches NTI 859 in FY2030 and 962 in FY2031 -- i.e. the Horizon 2030 '>EUR 1bn NTI' ambition arrives about a year late. Requires a sustained higher-volatility regime, APAC monetisation catching up with its +82% YTD value-traded growth, and a digital-assets recovery.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: PRE-SBC. Reported margins 38.9 / 40.6 / 42.3 / 43.6 / 44.7% from fixed opex 267 / 291 / 314 / 339 / 365 (prior bull path, +8-9%/yr funding the growth) and variable comp at 28% of NTI less fixed opex -- operating leverage carries the reported margin to the Horizon 2030 >45% level only by FY2031.
bull.lease_cost_note: Interest 20 / 19 / 18 / 17 / 17m (facilities amortise as earnings outgrow the fixed debt cost, as prior) + lease interest 1.6m, as % of NTI.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 12%/3% = 11.4x binds below the 13x cap. Prior bull used an 11% cost of equity; a single 12% is applied here (risk charged once).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 11x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged from the prior valuation (25/50/25). Bear at 25% rather than the 15% house default because the downside is not a tail: 3Q26 just delivered a drought quarter (NTI -43% QoQ, net profit EUR 6.4m) inside a year that began at record pace, the digital-assets segment is down 46% YTD, and fixed costs and interest are both structurally higher than in FY2023. Bull held at 25% because Horizon 2030 needs several independent things to go right (volatility regime, APAC monetisation, crypto recovery, cost discipline) and the balance sheet is now levered to deliver it. Base 50% is the mid-cycle outcome.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
